Date Time Picker

The Date Time Picker combines the Calendar and the Time Picker in one popup. Choose a day, then set hours and minutes using the spinners, and confirm with Apply.

Basic Date Time Picker

Click the field, pick a day, adjust the time and press Apply. Clear resets the selection and Now snaps to the current instant.

Nothing selected yet.

HTML
<div class="zak-datetime-picker">
    <button type="button" class="zak-datetime-field">
        <span class="zak-datetime-value">Pick date &amp; time</span>
    </button>
    <div class="zak-datetime-popup">
        <div class="zak-calendar">  <!-- month grid --> </div>
        <hr class="zak-datetime-divider">
        <div class="zak-datetime-time">  <!-- hour + minute spinners --> </div>
        <div class="zak-datetime-footer">
            <button class="zak-btn zak-btn-sm">Clear</button>
            <button class="zak-btn zak-btn-primary zak-btn-sm">Apply</button>
        </div>
    </div>
</div>

Two Fields, One Intent

For forms, keep two hidden inputs (date + time) and rebuild the full value from them. This mirrors how Date Picker and Time Picker submit independently.

HTML
<input type="hidden" name="scheduled_at">

<script>
    function commit(d, h, m) {
        var pad = function (n) { return ('0' + n).slice(-2); };
        var iso = d.getFullYear() + '-' + pad(d.getMonth() + 1) + '-' + pad(d.getDate()) +
                  'T' + pad(h) + ':' + pad(m);
        form.scheduled_at.value = iso;      // "2026-09-08T14:30"
        field.textContent = short(d, h, m);
    }
</script>

Minute Stepping

Minutes step by five in both columns, matching the standalone Time Picker convention. Hours wrap 0–23.

CSS Classes

HTML
// Date Time Picker composition:
.zak-datetime-picker    /* Relative wrapper (field + popup) */
.zak-datetime-field     /* Readable trigger */
.zak-datetime-popup     /* Popup holding calendar + time */
.zak-datetime-divider   /* Rule between date and time */
.zak-datetime-time      /* Spinner assembly */
.zak-datetime-footer    /* Clear / Apply action row */

// Reused primitives:
.zak-calendar, .zak-calendar-day, .zak-calendar-day.zak-selected ...
.zak-timepicker-column, .zak-timepicker-spin-up/down,
.zak-timepicker-hour/minute, .zak-timepicker-separator ...
.zak-btn, .zak-btn-primary, .zak-btn-sm

// Toggle class:
.zak-datetime-popup-active   /* Shows the popup */

JavaScript

HTML
// No library module — compose the Calendar and Time helpers:

var state = { date: null, hour: 9, min: 0 };

function drawCalendar() { /* build .zak-calendar grid (see Calendar) */ }
function drawTime() {
    // re-read state.hour / state.min into the spinners
}

cal.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
    var day = e.target.closest('.zak-calendar-day');
    if (!day || day.classList.contains('zak-outside')) return;
    state.date = new Date(day.getAttribute('data-date'));
    drawCalendar(); drawTime();
});

function bump(spin, value, max, wrap) {      // clamp to range
    value += spin;
    if (value < 0) value = wrap ? max : 0;
    if (value > max) value = wrap ? 0 : max;
    return value;
}

applyBtn.onclick = function () { commit(state.date, state.hour, state.min); };

Accessibility

  • The trigger is a <button>; days and spinner arrows are buttons too, so everything is focusable.
  • Announce the committed value with an aria-live region rather than only updating the field text.
  • Group the two hidden values under one label (e.g. Scheduled at) so the date+time reads as a unit.
  • Let Esc or backdrop click cancel so a half-finished selection never submits.
